auditor.opinionText: The consolidated financial statements present fairly, in all material respects, the consolidated financial position of the Group as at 31 December 2024, in accordance with IFRS as endorsed in the Kingdom and SOCPA pronouncements.
auditor.materiality: Not disclosed in the auditor's report

kams.title: Inventory valuation
kams.summary: Inventory of SAR 704.6 million (2023: SAR 900.3 million) is stated after a provision of SAR 124.5 million (2023: SAR 113.8 million) for slow-moving, obsolete and damaged items. Establishing the provision involves significant management judgement.

auditor.otherMatter: The 2023 financial statements were audited by another auditor who expressed a QUALIFIED opinion on 23 March 2024: including land in the Ceramic Pipes Company cash-generating unit was considered inconsistent with IAS 36, and excluding it would have increased the 2023 impairment loss and net loss by SAR 68 million. The current auditor concluded that including the land in the CGU is in line with IAS 36.

brief:
Saudi Ceramic narrowed its net loss to SAR 79,252 thousand (2023: SAR 237,519 thousand) on revenue of SAR 1,348,797 thousand, up 2.6% [[n:20]]. The improvement is largely the absence of 2023's fire-related impairments (SAR 136,880 thousand of plant and SAR 27,964 thousand of inventory) [[n:32]], but the Group still booked SAR 51,070 thousand of impairments: SAR 45 million on the Red Bricks unit and SAR 5.7 million on Ceramic Pipes Company, which management intends to liquidate after 2027 [[n:5]].

Operating cash flow more than doubled to SAR 312,791 thousand as inventories were cut by SAR 152,131 thousand [[n:9]], yet total borrowings remain high at SAR 735,845 thousand against equity of SAR 1,424,700 thousand, and SAR 516,805 thousand falls due within one year [[n:16]] [[n:30]]. The Group breached the debt-service cover ratio on a SAR 45 million short-term loan [[n:16]].

PKF Al-Bassam's 2024 opinion is unmodified, but the predecessor auditor qualified the 2023 opinion and comparatives were restated [[n:33]]. Reviewers should examine the SIDF mortgage over SAR 379 million of plant [[n:5]], customer concentration (five customers = 39% of revenue, 47% of receivables) [[n:26]] [[n:30]], the pending fire-insurance claim [[n:32]] and negative net assets at the 77.89%-owned Ceramic Pipes subsidiary [[n:31]].

lens.headline: Listed joint stock company with SAR 1,000 million share capital (100 million shares) after a 25% bonus issue; three subsidiaries, two not yet operating.
lens.detail: Ceramic Pipes Company is 77.89% owned (up from 73.89% after a 4% waiver by shareholder Khaled Saleh Abdulaziz Al Rajhi in July 2024); Arzan Company (100%) and Ceramics Investment Company (98.69%) had not started commercial operations by year-end. The statutory reserve of SAR 241,715 thousand was released to retained earnings after by-law amendments.

lens.headline: Second consecutive net loss (SAR 79,252 thousand) and an operating loss of SAR 82,647 thousand; management concludes the Group remains a going concern.
lens.detail: The ceramic tiles and sanitary ware segment lost SAR 83,872 thousand before zakat and Ceramic Pipes lost SAR 33,171 thousand; only water heaters were profitable (SAR 45,849 thousand). Other income of SAR 57,616 thousand (training support, asset sales, zakat reversal) cushioned the result. Note 3 states management has no material doubts about the Group's ability to continue as a going concern.

lens.headline: Borrowings of SAR 735,845 thousand with SAR 516,805 thousand due within one year; debt-service cover ratio breached on a SAR 45 million short-term loan.
lens.detail: Short-term Murabaha/Tawarruq loans rose to SAR 405,855 thousand (SIBOR + 1%). Long-term facilities include SIDF loans of SAR 114,343 thousand secured by a mortgage over land, buildings and plant with a book value of SAR 379 million, and bank loans at EIBOR + 0.9%. In 2023 subsidiary CPC breached loan terms and its non-current debt was reclassified as current. A 100 bp rise in commission rates would cost SAR 5,590 thousand.

lens.headline: SAR 51,070 thousand of impairments: Red Bricks unit (SAR 45 million, fair value less costs of disposal) and Ceramic Pipes (SAR 5.7 million, value in use at 12% with liquidation intended after 2027).
lens.detail: 2023 carried SAR 78,224 thousand of CPC impairment plus SAR 136,880 thousand fire damage. Inventory provisions rose to SAR 124,554 thousand (15% of gross inventory) after a SAR 43,548 thousand charge. The predecessor auditor qualified the 2023 opinion over the CPC land included in the CGU.

lens.headline: The July 2023 fire destroyed SAR 136.8 million of machinery and SAR 27.9 million of inventory; the insurance claim was still under evaluation at the reporting date.
lens.detail: Management believes coverage (including business interruption) is sufficient, but no insurance recovery has been recognised. Damaged inventory of SAR 27.96 million was written off against the 2023 provision during 2024.

lens.headline: Five largest customers account for ~39% of revenue and ~47% of trade receivables; SAR 33,055 thousand of receivables is more than 270 days past due.
lens.detail: Gross trade receivables of SAR 308,668 thousand carry an expected-credit-loss allowance of SAR 21,483 thousand and a customers'-incentive provision of SAR 65,207 thousand. 86.2% of receivables are in KSA and 13.6% in other GCC states. Receivables fell SAR 30,617 thousand during the year.

lens.headline: Revenue is 92% domestic (SAR 1,243,403 thousand); exports fell to SAR 105,394 thousand. All PP&E is located in Saudi Arabia.
lens.detail: Three reportable segments: ceramic tiles and sanitary ware (SAR 899,748 thousand), water heaters (SAR 429,828 thousand) and ceramic pipes (SAR 19,221 thousand). Revenue is recognised at a point in time; GCC exports were SAR 81,742 thousand and other countries SAR 23,652 thousand.

lens.headline: Capex of SAR 203,034 thousand, mainly a new porcelain tile factory funded by SIDF; assets under construction reached SAR 351,889 thousand.
lens.detail: Borrowing costs of SAR 9.1 million were capitalised. Letters of credit of SAR 7 million cover remaining machinery commitments for plant expansion. Intangible assets of SAR 6,643 thousand were acquired for the first time.

lens.headline: Purchases of SAR 45,631 thousand from affiliates (mainly Natural Gas Distribution Company); board and executive remuneration SAR 11,102 thousand.
lens.detail: The remaining 2.38% stake in Natural Gas Distribution Company was sold in 2024 for SAR 5.1 million (gain SAR 3.8 million). Balances with affiliates of SAR 3,988 thousand sit in trade payables.

lens.headline: Zakat expense SAR 8,058 thousand after a SAR 4,858 thousand reversal; ZATCA final assessments for 2021–2022 produced SAR 3.9 million of differences, accepted and paid.
lens.detail: Assessments are closed to 2022 for the parent and to 2018 for Ceramic Pipes Company; the 2023 returns have not yet been assessed. Zakat paid during the year was SAR 26,379 thousand.

lens.headline: 2023 comparatives were restated: receivables reduced by SAR 62,802 thousand, payables by SAR 74,325 thousand, and accrued finance costs moved into borrowings.
lens.detail: The restatement reclassified customer-incentive provisions, foreign-exchange differences and customer advances; it had no effect on the 2023 result or equity. Depreciation of leasehold improvements was also changed prospectively (SAR 2.3 million lower expense).

lens.headline: PKF Al-Bassam issued an unmodified 2024 opinion with one key audit matter, but the 2023 statements carried a qualified opinion from the predecessor auditor.
lens.detail: Statements were approved by the Board on 24 February 2025; the audit report is dated 3 March 2025. No subsequent events requiring adjustment were identified. Audit and review fees were SAR 625,000.
